subsystems.name: Telescope and adaptive optics
subsystems.role: delivers a stable, diffraction-limited image so faint planet light is not buried in atmospheric blur.

subsystems.name: Coronagraph and starlight suppression
subsystems.role: blocks the bulk of the host star's light before it reaches the polarimeter.

subsystems.name: Polarimetry module
subsystems.role: splits the beam into two orthogonal polarisation states and encodes the Stokes parameters.
parts: achromatic half-wave plate on a precision rotation stage
calibration unit injecting known polarisation states

subsystems.name: Spectrograph
subsystems.role: disperses the planet's light at a resolving power of a few hundred to a few thousand so cloud features are separable across wavelength.

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: records both polarisation beams simultaneously with low noise and short exposure times.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline and scattering model
subsystems.role: converts raw frames into polarisation spectra and fits them to cloud physics.

buildSteps.title: Pick the target and bandpass
buildSteps.detail: Choose a giant planet on a wide, well-separated orbit so it clears the inner working angle, and a wavelength range where reflected starlight competes least with the star's own colour.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical train
buildSteps.detail: Lay out adaptive optics, coronagraph and polarimeter so the polarising optics sit downstream of the coronagraph, where scattered starlight is already reduced.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the polarimeter
buildSteps.detail: Build an achromatic retarder stack that keeps a half-wave shift across the whole bandpass, pair it with a beam-splitter, and mount both on a stage that can index accurately to a fraction of a degree.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the high-contrast imager
buildSteps.detail: Insert the module into an existing extreme-adaptive-optics instrument, keeping the two polarisation beams on the detector simultaneously so atmospheric and telescope fluctuations cancel.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate instrumental polarisation
buildSteps.detail: Observe unpolarised standard stars to map the polarisation the telescope mirrors impose, and polarised standards to fix the angle offset and efficiency; repeat regularly because mirror coatings age.

buildSteps.title: Observe a polarisation sequence
buildSteps.detail: Take rapid exposures with the waveplate stepped through several angles, nodding the star between the two beams, and repeat across the planet's orbital phase or across the transit.

buildSteps.title: Reduce to Stokes spectra
buildSteps.detail: Subtract the two beams to cancel unpolarised starlight, combine waveplate angles into Stokes Q and U, then de-rotate by the parallactic angle and bin into a spectrum.

buildSteps.title: Fit cloud and haze parameters
buildSteps.detail: Compare the polarisation spectrum and its phase dependence against radiative-transfer models that vary particle size, composition, shape and cloud-top pressure.

buildSteps.title: Cross-check against intensity spectra
buildSteps.detail: Combine the polarimetric result with ordinary spectroscopy, since a liquid-surface glint and a thin haze can look similar in intensity alone but differ strongly in polarisation.

prerequisites.why: without roughly 10⁻⁵ starlight suppression the planet's few-percent polarisation is swamped.
the polarisation state must stay accurately defined across the bandpass or the spectrum is corrupted.
mirror-induced polarisation currently limits how faint a polarised signal can be trusted.

prerequisites.tech: Polarised radiative-transfer models of planetary atmospheres
prerequisites.why: Rayleigh and Mie scattering are well understood, but real haze particles are irregular and their scattering matrices are poorly constrained.

prerequisites.tech: Large filled-aperture telescopes with polarimetric modes
prerequisites.why: collecting area sets how bright a target must be; only a handful of facilities offer the combination.

pathway.milestone: polarimetric differential imaging routinely maps scattered light in circumstellar disks with current high-contrast instruments
pathway.unlocks: proven hardware and reduction techniques that can be pointed at planets.

pathway.milestone: dedicated polarimetric modes with rigorous calibration reach the brightest hot Jupiters and young, widely separated giants
pathway.unlocks: the first robust polarisation spectra of an exoplanet atmosphere.

pathway.milestone: 30 m class telescopes add collecting area and spectral resolution
pathway.unlocks: polarisation phase curves for a small sample of planets, separating cloud decks from clear atmospheres.

pathway.milestone: space-based coronagraphs combine high-resolution spectroscopy with polarimetry on temperate planets
pathway.unlocks: discriminating hazes, clouds and specular glints from liquid surfaces, which sharpens the interpretation of any biosignature.
